# Additive tuning of 2026-10-24, base re-measure of scenario 3

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:cd4a129e2acc3a76d856cec427c5e93dcec1dc28f47cfa0f4ef1e00c2dee24cc
lock: sha256:7b9b260a20cfe3c7b36337353499537aa39963f4be464ebcc9f28e55773eef36
selection: sha256:8d4747a05d1213146c97d37a574a457ce8aeee431a3f9f6a9c67c79021d1f437
read_set: sha256:f18e4fd7eafa09aabd6204d8a41112a4af8892eb03c0b5d7fb9d3bf5f927b3a3
seed: 0
harness: 0.6.1
tier: additive
arm: scenario-3
at: 2026-10-23
cost_cents: 10327
```

**This line is the first `base` stage of the tuning round of the additive campaign, which [#1777](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1777) asked for.** [#1838](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1838) added the stage: before a confirmation, the round measures the base scenario again at the confirmation's count and at the variant's commit. This line measures scenario 3, the base of round 1 of the skills layer, which [#1855](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1855) opened at `bea46653` to compare scenario 4 against scenario 3. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-3 tuning`. It is the `scenario-3` arm of the additive tier over 5 probes of the tuning set, at 29 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `bea46653` for the whole batch. The canary of 8 sessions held 4 records that named paths outside the workspace, and these records were read before `canary-passed` was written. The driver then halted twice at 28 of 145 sessions, and it continued in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 145 sessions and cost 10327 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 2 stopped at the turn cap, 0 stopped at the session budget, 77 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 3 passed 76 of 145 sessions. The base row compares this measurement with the screening measurement of scenario 3 on 2026-10-18, which passed 40 of 72 in [the screening transcript](additive-screening-of-2026-10-18-scenario-3.md). The difference is -3.1 points, with the interval [-16.7, +10.8]. The interval includes zero, so this measurement shows no change from the screening. The keep rule does not read a base, and a base is never kept. `try.sh result` wrote `3 bea46653` to the base pin, and a confirmation of the skills layer reads that pin.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,512.00 for the whole tuning round, over every attempt and every layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 12250 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 10606 cents against its cap, and the 145 recorded sessions account for 10327 cents of that sum. The 10606 cents go against the base ceiling of 22000 cents in `.headwater/probe.yml`, and not against the ceiling of 129000 cents for the tries. [#1854](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1854) declared that base ceiling for the bases of the layers that [#1833](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1833) set, and this line is the first charge to it.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1777/base-1/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.
